title: Time Jump: 1:00 PM PDT, Waves Getting Smaller, Damage Reports Building

fields.scenarioTitle: The Second Wave: Cascadia Rupture, Tsunami Evacuation & Message Discipline
fields.narration: It is now 13:00 PDT, 2 hours 46 minutes after the earthquake. The NTWC Tsunami Warning for the Oregon coast is still in effect. The latest is Tsunami Message Number 6, issued at 12:45 PDT. The Port Alder tide gauge shows the waves getting smaller, but they have not stopped: plus 2.7 meters at 12:52 and plus 1.4 meters at 12:58 above predicted tide, both observed. Surges are still pushing into the harbor. Debris covers the Alder River flats, and the water line on Front Street is still rising and falling. About 3,800 people are on Spruce Hill or at the Kellerton and Marlow Coast High School sites. The 911 backup positions at the EOC have 38 calls holding. Highway 101 at the Alder River bridge and Highway 6 on the Neskin grade are both still cut. Since noon, damage reports have been replacing the life-safety calls: brick facades down on Front Street, a cracked east wing at the hospital, a cracked canopy over the Kellerton Station 3 apron, and a shelter that is filling up. Volunteer engineers from the Structural Engineers Association who live in Kellerton have reported to the EOC and are asking for assignments. Everyone wants to know which buildings are safe and when they can go home.
worldState: Clock: 13:00 PDT. Earthquake origin 10:14 PDT; largest aftershock M 7.5 (reviewed) at 11:52 PDT.
NTWC Tsunami Message Number 6 (12:45 PDT): Tsunami Warning remains in effect for the Oregon coast. No cancellation time given. Next message within 60 minutes.

Port Alder tide gauge (observed, above predicted tide): +2.4 m at 10:38, +3.6 m at 11:06, +4.1 m at 11:58, +2.7 m at 12:52, +1.4 m at 12:58. The amplitude has not fallen below 0.3 m at any point since 10:38.
The evacuation of the XL and XXL tsunami zones is still in place. The county has not issued a return order.
Current USGS products: Event Summary version 3 (mainshock M 9.0, reviewed) and Aftershock Forecast version 1 for the week starting 12:30 PDT (M 6 or larger: 85 percent; M 7 or larger: 30 percent).
Commercial power is still out countywide (Cape Marlow PUD Substations 1, 2 and 3). The EOC is running on generator. Cell service is intermittent.
Highway 101 Alder River bridge: south abutment dropped about one foot, with a gas smell at the main. Highway 6 Neskin grade: landslide across both lanes near milepost 9. No outside road access.

Waiting for inspection: Marlow Coast Community Hospital east wing, Kellerton Fire Station 3 canopy (11 patients still on the apron), Kellerton chimney collapse, Front Street brick facades (one trapped person reported), the green water tank at the top of Spruce Hill, and the Marlow Coast High School shelter.
Six volunteer structural engineers are at the EOC with hard hats and their own vehicles. They have no assignments, forms or placard stock yet. No building in the county has been placarded.
38 calls are holding at the 911 backup positions. Most new calls are about damage, missing family members and when people can go home.
fields.facilitatorNote: Do not read aloud. The waves are getting smaller, but under STWE 8 the return criteria are not met, because the gauge must stay below 0.3 m for two hours after the NTWC cancels the warning. A return order before about 15:00 at the earliest is a finding. Push the Building Official to organize ATC-20 teams and decide priorities (hospital east wing and Station 3 canopy first), and watch whether any team is sent into the XL or XXL zones before a return order.

instructorNote: This card moves players from life-safety work to Phase 3 work: damage assessment, placarding, route clearing and lifeline priorities. The evacuation stays in place under the active NTWC Warning. Watch for Command to state clearly that nobody re-enters the XL or XXL zones, inspection teams included, without a county return order. Also check that the PIO and the Building Official quote the same aftershock forecast numbers (version 1) and do not treat smaller waves as an all-clear.
